A true base rate behind a noisily recorded one

Source: R/nsbnd.R
nsbnd.Rd

A recorded outcome is often a proxy: a rearrest for a reoffence, a recorded crime for one committed. With false-positive noise a, the chance a case without the outcome is recorded with it, and false-negative noise b, the chance a case with it is not, a true base rate p is recorded as pobs = p (1 - b) + (1 - p) a. Given only the boxes the noise rates lie in, nsbnd() gives the interval of true rates consistent with each recorded rate, and says for each pair of groups whether the order of their true rates follows from the records whatever the noise.

Usage

nsbnd(pobs, a, b)

Arguments

pobs

Recorded rates: numbers from 0 to 1, named or not.

a

The box of the false-positive noise rate: one number a (the box from 0 to a) or two, its ends; from 0.

b

The box of the false-negative noise rate, in the same way. The upper ends of a and b must add to less than 1.

Value

A list: bnd, a data frame with one row per rate: rate (its name, or its position), pobs, lo, hi and width; pairs, one row per pair i before j: i, j, ord ("lower": i's true rate is below j's for every admissible noise; "higher"; "undecided"; NA when either has no interval) and bd (NA when the rates are equal or no box keeps them ordered).

Details

The true rate (pobs - a) / (1 - a - b) falls as a grows and rises as b grows, so its ends are reached at corners of the boxes: the lower at the largest a (capped at pobs) and smallest b, the upper at the smallest a and largest b (capped at 1 - pobs). Both ends are attained, so no narrower interval follows from the boxes alone; with known noise rates (each box one point) the interval is the one true rate. A recorded rate that no admissible noise can produce (below the smallest a, or above 1 - the smallest b) has no interval (NaN).

Two groups' true rates are ordered whatever the noise exactly when their intervals do not overlap; when they overlap there is admissible noise under which either is the larger. bd is the largest upper end of the b box, a held, at which the lower recorded rate's interval stays below the other's: how much under-recording the order survives. The boxes are the analyst's claim about how the records were made; the bounds are only as good as that claim. See proof("nsbnd").

References

Fogliato, R., Chouldechova, A. and G'Sell, M. (2020). Fairness evaluation in presence of biased noisy labels. Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR 108, 2325-2336. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2003.13808

Examples

# rearrest rates of two groups; up to 10% false positives, 20% missed
nsbnd(c(a = 0.35, b = 0.55), a = 0.10, b = 0.20)
#> $bnd
#>   rate pobs        lo     hi     width
#> 1    a 0.35 0.2777778 0.4375 0.1597222
#> 2    b 0.55 0.5000000 0.6875 0.1875000
#> 
#> $pairs
#>   i j   ord  bd
#> 1 a b lower 0.3
#> 
# with up to 40% missed, the order is no longer identified
nsbnd(c(a = 0.35, b = 0.55), a = 0.05, b = 0.40)$pairs
#>   i j       ord    bd
#> 1 a b undecided 0.335
# known noise rates give the true rate itself
nsbnd(0.4 * 0.8 + 0.6 * 0.1, a = c(0.1, 0.1), b = c(0.2, 0.2))$bnd
#>   rate pobs  lo  hi width
#> 1    1 0.38 0.4 0.4     0
